chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked him: When does ghusl become obligatory upon the man and the woman? He said: “When he inserts it, then ghusl, the mahr, and stoning have become obligatory.”

key_terms.أَدْخَلَهُ: he inserted it; the act identified as the cause of the ruling
key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man; one of the two legal subjects addressed in the ruling
key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning; a legal penal consequence mentioned in the text
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ghusl; the ritual bath that becomes obligatory after janabah
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman; the other legal subject addressed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory for a man and a woman according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal threshold at which ghusl becomes obligatory for both the man and the woman. It also links that act to related legal consequences, including the mahr and rajm, indicating the juridical significance of consummation in Islamic law.
